chapters.description: The body's first defenses keep many microbes out and respond quickly when a threat gets through.

lessons.canDo: Distinguish pathogens from harmless microbes
lessons.description: Pathogens are microbes that can cause illness, while many other microbes live with us without causing harm.
skills: Identify pathogens that can cause illness
lessons.title: Pathogens and harmless microbes

lessons.canDo: Describe how barriers block infection
lessons.description: Skin, mucus and other barriers stop many pathogens before immune cells need to respond.
lessons.title: Physical barriers to infection

lessons.canDo: Describe how innate defenses spot a threat
lessons.description: Early immune defenses detect common signs of microbes or damage without identifying a particular pathogen.
lessons.title: Innate immune detection

lessons.canDo: Explain how inflammation calls for help
lessons.description: Inflammation brings immune cells and protective substances to a threatened area, causing signs such as warmth and swelling.
lessons.title: Inflammation and immune alerts

lessons.canDo: Explain why inflammation needs to subside
lessons.description: Immune defenses must ease after a threat is controlled so their activity does not keep damaging healthy tissue.
lessons.title: Resolution of inflammation

objectives: Identify microbes that can cause illness
Describe how barriers and innate defenses respond to threats
Explain why inflammation must be controlled
chapters.title: Threats and early defenses

chapters.description: Targeted defenses use recognizable features of a threat to coordinate cells that make antibodies or remove infected cells.

lessons.canDo: Explain how antigens guide targeted defenses
lessons.description: Antigens are recognizable features that let immune cells respond to a particular threat.
lessons.title: Antigens and immune recognition

lessons.canDo: Describe how immune cells display antigens
lessons.description: Some immune cells display pieces of a threat so other immune cells can recognize it and respond.
lessons.title: Antigen presentation

lessons.canDo: Explain how helper T cells direct a response
lessons.description: After recognizing a presented antigen, helper T cells send signals that coordinate targeted defenses.
lessons.title: Helper T cell coordination

lessons.canDo: Describe how B cells start making antibodies
lessons.description: A B cell that matches an antigen can receive help that prompts it to make antibodies.
lessons.title: B cell activation

lessons.canDo: Explain how antibodies can prevent illness
lessons.description: Antibodies bind to matching targets and can block a pathogen or help other defenses clear it.
lessons.title: Antibody protection

lessons.canDo: Explain how killer T cells remove infected cells
lessons.description: Killer T cells recognize infected cells displaying a matching target and destroy those cells to limit infection.
lessons.title: Killer T cell responses

objectives: Explain how antigens make a targeted response possible
Describe how immune cells coordinate a targeted response
Compare antibody protection with the removal of infected cells
chapters.title: Targeted immune responses

chapters.description: Immune memory helps the body respond to familiar threats, and vaccines build that memory without requiring the disease itself.

lessons.canDo: Explain a faster response to a familiar threat
lessons.description: Some B and T cells remain after a response and can act more quickly when they meet the same threat again.
lessons.title: Immune memory

lessons.canDo: Explain how vaccines train immune defenses
lessons.description: Vaccines expose the immune system to an antigen or instructions for making one without requiring the disease itself.
lessons.title: Vaccine training

lessons.canDo: Compare broad ways vaccines supply a target
lessons.description: Vaccines may supply a weakened pathogen, an inactivated pathogen, a pathogen piece or instructions for making a piece.
lessons.title: Ways vaccines present antigens

lessons.canDo: Describe how messenger RNA vaccines supply instructions
lessons.description: Messenger RNA vaccines give cells temporary instructions to make a pathogen piece that the immune system can recognize.
lessons.title: Messenger RNA vaccines

lessons.canDo: Explain why another vaccine dose may help
lessons.description: A booster gives immune defenses another encounter with a target, which can strengthen or renew protection.
lessons.title: Booster doses

objectives: Compare ways vaccines train immune defenses
Describe why booster doses can renew protection
chapters.title: Immune memory and vaccination

chapters.description: Vaccine protection varies with the pathogen and the person, so outcomes and side effects need careful interpretation.

lessons.canDo: Explain how variants can weaken recognition
lessons.description: Changes to a pathogen can alter familiar antigens, making existing immune recognition less effective.
lessons.title: Pathogen variants and immune recognition

lessons.canDo: Explain why vaccination cannot prevent every infection
lessons.description: Immune protection is not an absolute barrier, even when it lowers the chance of illness or severe disease.
lessons.title: Breakthrough infections

lessons.canDo: Distinguish protection against infection from severe disease
lessons.description: A vaccine can have different effects on becoming infected, developing symptoms and becoming seriously ill.
lessons.title: Measures of vaccine protection

lessons.canDo: Relate individual protection to community spread
lessons.description: When enough people have protection against infection or transmission, a pathogen may have fewer chances to spread.
lessons.title: Vaccination and community protection

lessons.canDo: Explain common short-lived vaccine reactions
lessons.description: Soreness, fatigue and fever can occur as immune activity rises after vaccination and usually fade soon afterward.
lessons.title: Common vaccine reactions

lessons.canDo: Compare a vaccine's benefits and risks
lessons.description: A sound vaccine decision weighs the risks of the disease against expected protection and possible adverse effects.
lessons.title: Vaccine benefit and risk

objectives: Explain why protection can change as pathogens change
Distinguish infection from other vaccine outcomes
Interpret common reactions and weigh benefits against risks
chapters.title: The limits and effects of vaccine protection

chapters.description: Immune defenses can cause harm when misdirected or weakened, and newer treatments aim to redirect them more precisely.

lessons.canDo: Explain how an allergy misdirects protection
lessons.description: Allergies occur when immune defenses react to a usually harmless substance and cause symptoms.
lessons.title: Allergic responses

lessons.canDo: Explain how immunity can harm healthy tissue
lessons.description: Autoimmune disease develops when immune defenses attack the body's own tissues instead of leaving them alone.
lessons.title: Autoimmune disease

lessons.canDo: Describe what happens when immune defenses are weak
lessons.description: Immune deficiencies make some infections harder to prevent or clear, whether the weakness is inherited or acquired.
lessons.title: Immune deficiency

lessons.canDo: Explain why transplants can be rejected
lessons.description: Immune cells may recognize a donated organ as foreign, so transplant care must balance rejection against infection risk.
lessons.title: Transplant rejection

lessons.canDo: Describe how cancers escape immune attack
lessons.description: Some cancer cells avoid detection or dampen nearby immune activity, allowing a tumor to grow.
lessons.title: Cancer immune evasion

lessons.canDo: Explain the aim of checkpoint inhibitors
lessons.description: Checkpoint inhibitors lift certain restraints on immune cells so they may attack a cancer, though healthy tissue can also be affected.
lessons.title: Checkpoint inhibitors

lessons.canDo: Explain the aim of engineered T cell therapy
lessons.description: Engineered T cell therapies give a person's immune cells a new way to recognize some cancers, with benefits and serious risks to weigh.
lessons.title: Engineered T cell therapies

objectives: Distinguish overactive, misdirected and weakened immunity
Explain why transplanted tissue may be rejected
Describe how cancer therapies redirect immune defenses
chapters.title: Immune disorders and targeted therapies
